name: Glass of water
note: One safe drink. For someone whose only water comes from a muddy pond, a clean glass is where it starts.

name: Canteen
note: Clean water to carry through a morning at school or a day in the fields, instead of going without.

name: Pitcher
note: Most of the drinking water one person needs to get through a day.

name: Fish bowl
note: A full day of safe drinking water for one person, with some left to share.

name: Bucket
note: A day of drinking and cooking water for one person, without the walk to fetch it.

name: Jerry can
note: Everything one person needs for a day: water to drink, to cook with and to wash.

name: Kitchen sink
note: Two days of drinking, cooking and washing water for one person.

name: Aquarium
note: Four days of clean water for one person. Four days of not choosing between drinking and washing.

name: Wheelbarrow
note: A day of clean water for a whole family of five.

name: Bathtub
note: Ten days of clean water for one person. Long enough for a sick child to get well on safe water.

name: Rain barrel
note: Nearly two weeks of drinking, cooking and washing water for one person.

name: Horse trough
note: Almost a month of clean water for one person. A month of mornings spent in class, not at the river.

name: Paddling pool
note: Almost two months of clean water for one person, or ten days for a family of five.

name: Hot tub
note: A hundred days of clean water for one person. A whole dry season of safe drinking, cooking and washing.

name: Fire engine
note: Close to six months of clean water for one person, or one full day for a village of about 165 people.
